messages:
sam: :rotating_light: Seeing a spike in GPU allocation failures in ap-south1. Provisioner shows a lot of nodes in OOB-reboot after the BMC firmware push this morning.

sam: Quick snapshot: ~12 nodes entered OOB in the last 30m, nvme warmboot cycles on attach, and some pods stuck in Pending due to failed device plugins.

oncall-bot: Alert 169: oob-node-apse3-04 entered 'oob-reboot' (BMC v3.2.1) - uptime 00:05. Related alerts: nvme-warmboot x3, kubelet-deviceplugin error x7.

tess: copying runbook notes — if BMC firmware toggles secureboot flag we saw before, nodes can drop to PXE or partial boot. Can someone confirm if the rollout enabled secureboot-by-default?

michael: I saw the deploy PR; it flipped the `enable_secure_boot` flag for the ap-south1 OOB pool to true to match compliance. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/ops/4521

ryan: That matches. We scheduled v3.2.1 to ap-south1 at 02:15 UTC. Canary passed on 3 nodes, but looks like scale revealed NVMe driver fallback causing warmboots.

li: On the provisioning side, the fleet manager is retrying node attach which is saturating our serial jumphosts. Serial multiplex queues are rising, causing timeouts and more retries — positive feedback. We're seeing increased egress and a cost blip on jump-host proxy bandwidth.

sam: Can we pause the rollout and roll back the BMC image for the remaining nodes? Need to stop further churn.

michael: I've paused the remaining rollout steps in the deployment job and opened a rollback for the pool. `ci deploy cancel --job bmc-rollout-apse3` then `ci deploy rollback-image --pool ap-south1 --image v3.1.9`.

tess: Good. For the already-updated nodes, we should try a soft workaround: disable device plugin auto-reload and drain pods from affected nodes to reduce attach churn. `kubectl annotate node <node> deviceplugin.kubernetes.io/reload=false`

ryan: Draining is in progress for 6 nodes. Patch to the device plugin to ignore nvme device rescan while BMC is in-reboot is being prepared (small hotfix).

oncall-bot: Event: rollout paused by michael at 1719248287. Rollback job queued.

li: Note the cost impact: jump-host egress spiked ~45% over baseline during the last 40m because of repeated out-of-band console captures and node re-synchronization. If we keep retry loops long, we'll see a monthly delta. Filing a cost ticket.

sam: Filing ops-ticket now with logs and node list. Also capturing secureboot state across nodes: `ipmitool sel list` and `fw-ctl status` where available.

michael: For postmortem, let's capture: why canary didn't catch nvme warmboot path, why serial queue backpressure wasn't rate-limited, and whether the secureboot toggle interacts with NVMe drivers on these OEM firmwares.

tess: Agreed. Short-term: rollback remaining nodes, drain/restart affected nodes after rollback, and limit cross-pool serial concurrency to 10. I'll update runbook with the concurrency knob.

ryan: I've applied temporary concurrency cap on px-serial-proxy and cancelled some non-critical provisioning jobs. Monitoring for re-attaches.

oncall-bot: Node stabilization check at 1719248620: 9/12 previously-affected nodes returned to Ready within 18m after deviceplugin drain. 3 nodes still in OOB-reboot and assigned to manual investigation.

li: I'll drop the cost estimate into the ticket. Heads-up to finance: if this becomes a pattern we should consider a reserved jump-host bandwidth to cap spend.

sam: Thanks all. Next actions: michael finish rollback, tess update runbook + concurrency knob, ryan keep monitoring serial queue, li file cost ticket. We'll reconvene in #eng-infra if manual investigations surface hardware faults. :thumbsup:
